name: Whot Nigerian
description: Nigerian variant of Whot: a shedding game in the Eights family. Players match suit or number or play Whot (wild) and special cards (Hold On, Pick Two, Pick Three, Suspension, General Market). First to empty hand wins; penalty scoring over rounds. Popular in West Africa.

content.text: Nigerian variant of Whot: a shedding game in the Eights family. Players match suit or number or play Whot (wild) and special cards (Hold On, Pick Two, Pick Three, Suspension, General Market). First to empty hand wins; penalty scoring over rounds. Popular in West Africa.

Whot was invented by W.H. Storey in England in 1935 and became the national card game of Nigeria. Nigerian variant uses the same 54-card pack with local names for shapes (ball, angle, cross, carpet, star) and added special effects on 1, 2, 5, 8, and 14.

A 54-card Whot pack with five pictorial suits (circles, triangles, crosses, squares, stars) and five wild Whot cards numbered 20; this format is standard in Nigeria. Suit cards carry numbers 1–14 (not all numbers in every suit); star cards count double for scoring.
Dealer shuffles; player to dealer's right cuts. Dealer deals six cards to each player one at a time. Remainder forms a face-down draw pile (stock).

items.text: Short game: One deal only; first player to empty hand wins, no penalty scoring.
